subject: dragonling
pitch: A baby dragon the size of a house cat, sitting proudly beside the broken shell of its speckled egg. Teal scales fading to a buttery belly, stubby horns, a row of soft orange spines down its back, oversized wings it can't fly with yet, with translucent amber skin between the fingers, and a chubby tail ending in a little spade. Big amber eyes, a toothy grin and a wisp of smoke curling from one nostril.
reasoning:
I'm uncertain about exact API signatures beyond the documented reference, so I'll lean toward conservative, well-supported calls and fall back on plain three.js geometry where the SDK's options are unclear.

I'm weighing whether to attach plain meshes directly under named joints versus risking unknown chain/sweep arguments—since a crash matters more than rig fidelity, I'll use the SDK for joints and root structure, but build visible geometry with plain THREE meshes and flat-shaded materials, grouped under the joint hierarchy where possible.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton: hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, tail segments, legs, and wings, then designing the dragon's cat-sized sitting pose in model space—an ellipsoid body tilted back with a lighter belly patch, folded hind legs, and straight front legs, using a reusable mesh helper with cached colored materials.

For the head I'm placing a sphere with a protruding snout and lower jaw, plus small nostril spheres trailing curling smoke, amber eyes with pupils and highlights, backward-tilted horns, cheek spikes, and small teeth cones along the jaw. I'm connecting the neck with a cylinder, building the front legs as simple limb-and-foot shapes with toe cones, and shaping the hind legs with a thick thigh sphere and a forward foot with toes.

Now I'm curving the tail using a Catmull-Rom spline from the body outward, tapering spheres along it and finishing with a flat extruded spade shape oriented along the tail's tangent, then adding a row of orange back spines as shrinking cones following a curve from the neck down through the back to the tail.

For the wings, I'm building a folded-but-slightly-extended rest pose: shoulder-to-wrist arm bones, three radiating finger bones, and a translucent amber membrane stitched as a triangle fan connecting the body attachment points, wrist, finger tips, and hip attachment.

I'm positioning the finger tips and wrist with specific coordinates, then mirroring the whole wing across the body using a sign flip for the opposite side. Now I'm turning to the egg placed beside the creature, sketching its lower half using a partial sphere geometry.

For the egg's surface, I'm adding cream coloring with speckled dark dots stuck on as small flattened spheres, a jagged rim made of triangular cone shards pointing upward, plus a tilted loose shell fragment leaning nearby, and an inner yolk-colored liner sphere nested inside for depth.

Still working out shard cap geometry...

Now I'm picking the color palette: teal tones for the body and back, cream and amber for belly, horns, and claws, dark pupils, and a translucent grey-blue for smoke.

I'm adding belly striping with a few stacked ellipsoid bands in varying cream shades, a lighter throat patch, and scattering small flattened scale dots across the back and sides using randomized directions constrained away from the belly, oriented to match the body surface normal.

For the body itself, I'm defining an ellipsoid positioned and sized for a sitting torso, tilted slightly backward on the x-axis so the top leans away for a natural sitting posture, with the spot positions computed in local space before applying that same rotation.

For the scale dots, I'm orienting each one so its flat face points outward along the surface normal, using quaternion alignment from a default axis to that normal, then scaling them into tiny flattened spheres to mimic scales. For the head, I'm placing a slightly squashed sphere above the body with a boxy snout shape positioned at the front.

I'm detailing the mouth with an upper and lower jaw as separate boxes, a dark mouth line between them for the grin, small cone-shaped teeth along the snout edges pointing downward, a few upward teeth on the lower jaw, and tiny nostril spheres with a rising curl of smoke particles from one nostril.

Now I'm placing the eyes on the head's surface using distance offsets from center, giving each a flattened amber sphere, a dark vertical slit pupil ellipsoid, a small white highlight sphere, and considering a teal brow ridge above.

I'm positioning tilted cone horns near the top of the head, using rotation math to angle them backward and outward so they sweep away from the face naturally.

I'm also adding small fin-like ear frills to the sides of the head and a cheek bump, then setting up a neck cylinder oriented using a quaternion that aligns it between two points.

Now I'm defining the front legs with shoulder-elbow-hand joints, tapered rod segments, joint spheres, and clawed toes, plus starting the hind legs with a thigh sphere and foot shape.

I'm working out the shin segment positions and making sure foot bottoms rest near ground level, then mapping out the tail's curve as a series of points while checking it won't collide with the egg placed on the opposite side.

Still designing tail geometry...

Solving for the yaw angle gives me the orientation, placed at the tail's tangent position using nested groups, with the spade colored orange. Now I'm plotting the dragon's back spines as a sequence of points tracing from the neck down the body, defining the curve coordinates that follow the creature's spine profile.

Continuing this spine curve into the tail, I'm sizing the cones to taper from larger at the back to smaller toward the tip, orienting each one outward using estimated surface normals so they angle naturally away from the body and tail. Next I'll build helper functions for the wing finger bones using thin rods, plus the wrist joint and claw details.

I'm defining the wing membrane geometry now, specifying the amber translucent material and placing shoulder, elbow, wrist, and fingertip points per side, then triangulating a fan from the wrist point out to the fingertips and back attachment point to form the membrane surface.

I'm now setting up the full joint hierarchy — hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, tail segments, shoulders/elbows/wrists/fingers, and legs — with a small wrapper function to attach each joint to its parent, then assembling all the meshes into the root and preparing to write the material helper and final code.

Writing material helper...

Still positioning belly ellipsoid...

Adding under-jaw shading, teal gradient patches on the back, alternating darker and lighter dot colors, mirrored eye groups, and a rising nostril smoke effect with increasing radius and fading opacity...

For the egg, I'm scattering speckles across the bottom shell using randomized spherical coordinates with brown and teal colors, flattening them slightly and orienting each dot's normal based on the ellipsoid's scaled surface.

Then I'm adding a slightly smaller pale inner liner sphere and a cream-colored outer shell cap using a partial sphere geometry, working out the rim position by computing where the cap's cosine-based height aligns with the shell's center offset.

Adding a small tilt and a leaning wedge shard made from cones to add asymmetry, then double-checking the egg's bottom stays just above the ground plane before finalizing the code.
